question: Why does divine origin not make all scriptures equally binding in the same way?
premises: Even the Veda and other teachings were established by the Lord.
Nevertheless, they differ according to contraction, presence, absence, and alternative framing.
Their applicability varies with the condition of those they address.
inference: Although all such teachings may have divine origin, their scope and binding force differ according to levels of contraction and capacity.
uncertainties: The compound saṃkocabhāvābhāvavikalpataḥ is compressed and allows more than one technical unpacking.
plain_english: Although even the Veda and other teachings were established by the Lord, they still operate according to differences of contraction, presence, absence, and alternative application. For that reason, their force is not the same for everyone.
